provisioning_notes: Design catalogue only: no native item, spell, property, recipe, client route, live ID, SQL row, runtime hook, or craftability claim is admitted.

The eight field designs cover cloth chest, legs, head, shoulders, bracers, gloves, waist, and boots before auxiliary cloak work; their baseline is plain usable armor/stat allocation with no bespoke proc, action, or fatigue system, and they need no raid clear or multi-artisan monopoly.

Field, masterwork, and legendary role/stat envelopes are proposed per-item tuning budgets, not caps on separately earned boss legacies; exact numerical budgets, effects, proc rates, durations, cooldowns, ranges, and material quantities are unratified.

Caster DPS favors spell power, haste, and critical strike; healers favor healing power, resource regeneration, and haste. A commission selects a compatible envelope rather than receiving every stat at maximum.
Tailoring makes cloth and limited auxiliary cloaks/bags; it cannot make plate or offer unrestricted all-stat gear. Bags remain secondary to properly gearing adventurers.

Real ingredients, learned recipes, captured craft skill, character/profession level gates, city station eligibility, and funded commissions are prerequisites. Training and mastery are separate: mastery can qualify finishes but does not create free skill, XP, recipes, goods, or craftability.
Legendary candidates require an earned compatible boss core and admitted native route; each has exactly five sequential meaningful stages, with no claim that a stage is a usable item output.
Cloak collaboration is explicitly a child commission with its own qualified work, inputs, and settlement. A collaborator does not let a tailor produce plate or bypass a gate.
Exact native IDs and client behavior remain to be qualified by a future blueprint, input-settlement, craft, save/load, mail, equip, effect-observation, and removal proof.
